Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. Write $\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $P:W\to V$, and $Q:V\to W$. The Donaldson source convention for these four matrices is

$$[\alpha_1,\alpha_2]+PQ=0,\qquad [\alpha_1,\alpha_1^\dagger]+[\alpha_2,\alpha_2^\dagger]-PP^\dagger+Q^\dagger Q=0.$$

The second equality is an equality of Hermitian endomorphisms of $V$. It is an algebraic convention from the displayed source equations; it does not by itself assert the full-rank condition on the source's ADHM linear map or an identification with the run's raw moment maps.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

derivations.claim: Componentwise conjugation of $[\alpha_1,\alpha_2]+PQ=0$ gives $[\overline{\alpha_1},\overline{\alpha_2}]+\overline P\,\overline Q=0$. By [F2], this is exactly $\mu_{\mathbb C}(B,I,J)=0$.

Since $(\overline{\alpha_i})^\dagger=\overline{\alpha_i^\dagger}$, the commutator part of $\mu_{\mathbb R}$ is $\overline C$. Also $II^\dagger=\overline X$ and $J^\dagger J=\overline Y$. Thus $\mu_{\mathbb R}=\overline C+\overline X-\overline Y$. Conjugating the source real equation gives $\overline C-\overline X+\overline Y=0$, so the raw expression on such a source solution is $2(\overline X-\overline Y)=2\overline C$.

To verify that the source equations permit $C\ne0$, take $k=N=2$, $\alpha_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\alpha_2=0$, $P=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $Q=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$. Then $[\alpha_1,\alpha_2]+PQ=0$, $C=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, $X=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$, and $Y=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$, so $C-X+Y=0$. Under the proposed substitution the raw real moment map is $\operatorname{diag}(2,-2)\ne0$. This checks the claimed failure using only the source algebraic equations; it makes no claim that this tuple satisfies the separate source full-rank condition.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. A raw framed ADHM datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its complex and real moment expressions are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\geq0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable when no nonzero subspace of $V$ is invariant under both $B_1,B_2$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular when it is both stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ and its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set

$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable and costable}\}/U(V).$$

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\mathbb R^4=S^4\setminus\{\infty\}$ is $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\to S^4$, let $E=P\times_{U(N)}\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\Phi:E|_{\infty}\to\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature matrix and define

$$q_N(P,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The anti-self-dual equation is $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$. For integer $k\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\infty$ is the identity in the framing. This definition alone does not assert that every sector exists or that $q_N$ is integral; the exact $U(N)$ charge normalization is a separate lemma below.

Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a fixed right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$. The twistor space is $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, the projection $\pi:Z\to\mathbb H\mathbb P^1=S^4$ sends a complex line $\ell$ to the quaternionic line $\ell+j\ell$, and the antiholomorphic involution is $\sigma([v])=[jv]$. A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line. Fix homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ so $\sigma$ is induced by $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. The finite real line over $z$ has equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. These equations fix the quaternionic identification and its orientation. In the chart $\lambda_1=1,\lambda_2=0$, vertical complex orientation followed by the positive orientation of $(z_1,z_2)$ is the complex orientation of $Z$.


For the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\cong SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\ell\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Use the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric for the horizontal distribution of $\pi$; the horizontal $(0,1)$ subspace at $[\ell]\in L_x$ projects to this complex alpha-plane. The displayed orientation is the twistor orientation: the vertical complex orientation followed by the quotient orientation on $S^4$ agrees with the complex orientation on $Z$. It is chosen so the curvature component that vanishes on every such plane is precisely $F^+=(F+*_gF)/2$. In spinor components, $F_{AB}=F_{(AB)}$ denotes the symmetric spinor corresponding to $F^+$ under $\Lambda^2_+T_x^*S^4\otimes\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_x^+)^*$; restriction to the plane is $F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B$, which vanishes for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ exactly when $F^+=0$.

A linear monad on $Z$ is a complex of holomorphic bundles

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

where $U,U',K$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, $b\circ a=0$, $a$ is injective as a sheaf map, $b$ is surjective, and the cohomology sheaf $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ is locally free. It is framed when that cohomology has a specified unitary trivialization on $L_\infty$. For a holomorphic bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$ that is holomorphically trivial on every real line, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum is a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $b_z$ is complex linear in $u\in\mathcal E_z$ and conjugate linear in $v\in\mathcal E_{\sigma z}$; the conjugate pullback is holomorphic because $\sigma$ is antiholomorphic. For holomorphic sections $s,t$ on $L_x$, the function $b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ is holomorphic on the compact line, hence constant. It defines $h_x(s,t)$; require this Hermitian form to be positive definite for every $x$. The metric on each fibre of $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is transported from this form by holomorphic evaluation. Thus positive forms are induced by the pairing, not independent arbitrary choices. A framed Ward bundle includes a unitary framing on $L_\infty$ for this induced form. Smoothness and parallelness of the induced section-bundle metric are conclusions of the Ward construction.

The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acts on $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$ and on $W$ by $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its raw ADHM action is

$$ (t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ). $$

On the framed ASD sector, the same torus acts by inverse pullback under the indicated rotation of $S^4$ and by postcomposition of the framing with $h$. On $Z$, the rotations act by $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]\mapsto[\lambda_1:t_1t_2\lambda_2:t_1\mu_1:t_2\mu_2]$, equivalently the projective spin lift to $\mathbb P(S^+)$; the central sign in the spin double cover acts trivially after projectivization, and the induced action commutes with $\sigma$. The framing torus acts on the framed monad cohomology by the same diagonal representation.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a nonempty, connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with a supplied Riemannian metric. Let $G\subseteq U(V,h)$ be a compact non-Abelian matrix Lie group in its specified global form, let $\pi:P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle in a specified bundle sector (an isomorphism class of smooth principal bundles under isomorphisms over $X$), and let $\omega$ be a supplied smooth principal connection. Let $B:\mathfrak g\times\mathfrak g\to\mathbb R$ be a positive-definite symmetric bilinear form invariant under $\operatorname{Ad}(G)$. For local sections $s_i:U_i\to P$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$. If $F_i=\sum_a e_a F_i^a$ in a finite basis of $\mathfrak g$, define $B(F_i\wedge F_i):=\sum_{a,b}B(e_a,e_b)F_i^a\wedge F_i^b$; this expression is independent of the basis. Invariance of $B$ makes the local expressions $\beta_B|_{U_i}:=(8\pi^2)^{-1}B(F_i\wedge F_i)$ restrictions of a global four-form $\beta_B$. The **trace-normalized topological charge** is

$$
q_B(P,\omega):=\int_X\beta_B.
$$

The number $q_B(P,\omega)$ is independent of the supplied connection. For a general compact matrix group and invariant $B$, it is a real characteristic number; no integrality is asserted. In the special case $G=SU(2)$ in its defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$, with $h(v,w)=v^*w$ and $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_2(XY)$, the associated Hermitian bundle $E=P\times_{SU(2)}\mathbb C^2$ has

$$
q_B(P,\omega)=-\langle c_2(E),[X]\rangle\in\mathbb Z,
$$

where $c_2(E)\in H^4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the integral second Chern class and $[X]\in H_4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the orientation fundamental class. This sign is fixed by the library convention $c(E,\nabla)=\det(I-\Omega_\nabla/(2\pi i))$.

The Hodge operator $*_g$ on two-forms is characterized by $\alpha\wedge *_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$ and acts componentwise on $\mathfrak g$-valued forms. Set $F_i^+=(F_i+*_gF_i)/2$ and $F_i^-=(F_i-*_gF_i)/2$. The self-dual sector consists of connections with $F_i^-=0$, equivalently $F_i=*_gF_i$; the anti-self-dual (ASD) sector consists of connections with $F_i^+=0$, equivalently $F_i=-*_gF_i$. These conditions are independent of the local section.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle with a principal connection form $\omega$ associated to $H$, using $Z_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_0p\exp_G(tZ)$ for the right action. For Lie-algebra-valued forms use the graded bracket defined by alternating shuffle and the Lie bracket; in degree one, $[A\wedge B](X,Y)=[A(X),B(Y)]-[A(Y),B(X)]$. Define

$$\Omega_\omega:=d\omega+\frac12[\omega\wedge\omega],\qquad D_\omega\eta:=d\eta+[\omega\wedge\eta].$$

Then $\Omega_\omega$ is horizontal and $\operatorname{Ad}$-equivariant, and $\Omega_\omega=\omega\circ K_H$ for the imported vertical-valued curvature $K_H(X,Y)=-v([hX,hY])$. For any trivializing cover with smooth sections $s_i:U_i\to P$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=s_i^*\Omega_\omega$. On an overlap, let $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to G$ be the smooth map determined by $s_j=s_i g_{ij}$, and write $\theta_L(g_{ij})=g_{ij}^*\theta_L$ for the left Maurer–Cartan form. Then

$$A_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}A_i+\theta_L(g_{ij}),\qquad F_i=dA_i+\frac12[A_i\wedge A_i],\qquad F_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}F_i,\qquad D_{A_i}F_i=0,$$

where $D_{A_i}\eta:=d\eta+[A_i\wedge\eta]$. The transition equations concern changes of local sections; they do not identify an arbitrary map $M\to G$ with a global automorphism of a nontrivial bundle.
Assume countable choice. For $n\ge1$, $H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(S^n)$ is $\mathbb R$ in degrees $0,n$ and zero otherwise. For $S^0$ it is $\mathbb R^2$ in degree zero and zero otherwise.
For every natural number $n\ge2$, the unit sphere $S^n\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$ is simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]).

A connection on a finite-rank smooth vector bundle $E\to M$ is flat if and
only if every point of $M$ has a neighborhood carrying a local frame
$(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$ of parallel sections, meaning $\nabla_Xe_a=0$ for every
local vector field $X$ and every $a$.

Let $E\to M$ carry a flat connection, meaning $R^\nabla=0$. For every
$p\in M$ there is a coordinate ball $U$ about $p$ such that, whenever two
piecewise smooth paths $\gamma_0,\gamma_1:[0,1]\to U$ have the same initial
and terminal points,

$$P_{\gamma_0}=P_{\gamma_1}.$$

This is a local assertion; it makes no claim about transport around loops in a
non-simply-connected larger domain.

Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold,
possibly with boundary. If $E\to M$ is a rank-$r$ complex vector bundle with
complex connection $\nabla$ and curvature $\Omega$, define the total Chern form
$$c(\nabla)=\det\!\left(I-\frac{\Omega}{2\pi i}\right)=\sum_{j=0}^r c_j(\nabla),$$
where $c_j(\nabla)$ has degree $2j$. For a Hermitian connection these forms
are real-valued; a general complex connection need not give real-valued forms.

For a rank-$r$ real vector bundle with real connection $\nabla$, let
$E_{\mathbb C}=E\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ carry the complexified
connection $\nabla_{\mathbb C}$ and set
$$p_j(\nabla)=(-1)^j c_{2j}(\nabla_{\mathbb C})\quad\text{in degree }4j,\qquad p(\nabla)=\sum_{j\geq0}p_j(\nabla).$$
Then $p_0=1$, $p_j=0$ when $2j>r$, and every $p_j(\nabla)$ is real-valued,
even if $\nabla$ is not metric-compatible. If $\nabla$ is compatible with a
Euclidean metric, each odd Chern form $c_{2j+1}(\nabla_{\mathbb C})$ vanishes
pointwise. Assume full Axiom of Choice (AC); for every real connection each
$c_{2j+1}(\nabla_{\mathbb C})$ is then exact, with AC used through existence
of a metric-compatible connection and the transgression lemma.

If $E$ is an oriented Euclidean bundle of even rank $2m$ and $\nabla$ is
metric-compatible, define
$$e(\nabla)=\operatorname{Pf}\!\left(\frac{\Omega}{2\pi}\right),$$
where the Pfaffian uses the ordered oriented orthonormal frame and
$\operatorname{Pf}\!\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&a\\-a&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)=a$.
These curvature evaluations are closed forms. In rank zero,
$c(\nabla)=p(\nabla)=e(\nabla)=1$. The Euler form is defined here only for
oriented even-rank Euclidean bundles with a metric-compatible connection.

Assume AC. Let $E\to B$ be a numerable complex rank-$n$ bundle with $n\geq1$
over a path-connected CW complex $B$ (or over one of the CW-type bases of
[[thm-integral-complex-projective-bundle-theorem]]). By that theorem there are
unique classes $a_i\in H^{2i}(B;\mathbb Z)$, $1\leq i\leq n$, such that
$$x_E^{\,n}-a_1x_E^{\,n-1}+a_2x_E^{\,n-2}-\cdots+(-1)^na_n=0\qquad\text{in }H^{2n}(P(E);\mathbb Z),$$
where $x_E\in H^2(P(E);\mathbb Z)$ is the Euler class of the underlying real
bundle of the tautological line
([[def-complex-projective-bundle-and-tautological-complex-line]]). The
**Chern classes** of $E$ are these coefficients:
$$c_i(E):=a_i\in H^{2i}(B;\mathbb Z)\qquad(1\leq i\leq n),$$
completed by the conventions $c_0(E):=1\in H^0(B;\mathbb Z)$ and
$c_i(E):=0$ for $i>n$, and the **total Chern class** is the finite sum
$c(E):=\sum_{i\geq0}c_i(E)=1+c_1(E)+\cdots+c_n(E)\in H^*(B;\mathbb Z)$.

For the zero bundle of rank $0$ the conventions give $c(0_B)=1$. The definition
depends only on the isomorphism class of $E$, because an isomorphism of
bundles induces an isomorphism of projective bundles pulling $x$ back to $x$
and hence preserves the unique relation. For a complex line bundle $L\to B$ one
has $P(L)\cong B$ over $B$ with $\gamma_L$ corresponding to $L$ under that
identification, so the relation is $x_L-c_1(L)=0$; since $x_L=e(L_{\mathbb R})$
under the identification, this gives
$$c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R}).$$
This is the normalization used throughout the page: the first Chern class of a
complex line is the Euler class of its underlying real bundle in the complex
orientation, not a separately chosen normalization.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Hausdorff
second-countable smooth manifold, possibly with boundary or empty, and let
$\rho_M:H^*(M;\mathbb Z)\to H^*(M;\mathbb R)$ be induced by
$\mathbb Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb R$. Write $J_M$ for the natural de Rham
isomorphism from real de Rham cohomology to singular cohomology with real
coefficients.

For every finite-rank smooth complex bundle $E\to M$ with a Hermitian metric
and Hermitian connection $\nabla$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([c_j(\nabla)])=\rho_M(c_j(E)).$$
For every finite-rank smooth real bundle $V\to M$ with any real connection
$D$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([p_j(D)])=\rho_M(p_j(V)).$$
For every oriented Euclidean bundle $W\to M$ of even rank with a
metric-compatible connection $\nabla$, and its Thom-normalized Euler class,
$$J_M([e(\nabla)])=\rho_M(e(W)).$$
Here $c_j(\nabla)$, $p_j(D)$, and $e(\nabla)$ use the normalizations in
[[def-chern-pontryagin-and-euler-characteristic-forms]], while $c_j(E)$,
$p_j(V)$, and $e(W)$ are the published topological classes. In particular
$c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for a complex line and
$p_j(V)=(-1)^j c_{2j}(V_{\mathbb C})$. These are equalities after passage to
real coefficients; no equality with integral torsion is asserted.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold $M$, possibly with boundary, integration on smooth simplices followed by the inverse of restriction from continuous to smooth singular cohomology gives a natural isomorphism of unital graded real algebras
$$J_M:H^*_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^*_{\mathrm{sing}}(M;\mathbb R).$$
The source product is wedge of form classes, the target product is the front/back singular cup product, and both stars denote direct sums of the homogeneous groups. Naturality is for smooth maps. No compactness assumption is imposed.

derivations.claim: In a local unitary frame let $F_{\det A}$ be the curvature of the induced connection on $\det E$. The induced connection on the top exterior power has local connection matrix $\operatorname{tr}A$, hence $F_{\det A}=\operatorname{tr}F_A$. Put $\eta=-i\operatorname{tr}F_A$, a real two-form because $F_A$ is anti-Hermitian. By [F2], $d\eta=0$, and the linearity of trace in $F_A^+=0$ gives $*_g\eta=-\eta$.

By [A1] and [F3], $\eta$ is exact, so choose a smooth real one-form $\alpha$ with $\eta=d\alpha$. The ASD equation gives $\int_{S^4}\eta\wedge *_g\eta=-\int_{S^4}d\alpha\wedge\eta=-\int_{S^4}d(\alpha\wedge\eta)=0$, since $d\eta=0$ and $S^4$ is compact without boundary. The integrand $\eta\wedge *_g\eta$ is the nonnegative squared norm density of the real form $\eta$; zero integral forces $\eta=0$ pointwise. Hence $F_{\det A}=0$ and the determinant connection is flat.

Choose the unit vector $v_\infty$ in $(\det E)_\infty$ specified by the determinant of the framing. For any $x\in S^4$, parallel transport $v_\infty$ along a piecewise smooth path from $\infty$ to $x$. If two paths are chosen, their concatenation is a loop. By [F3] the loop is null-homotopic; subdivide a null-homotopy square into finitely many rectangles mapped into coordinate balls, which is possible by compactness and a Lebesgue number for the pulled-back coordinate-ball cover. On each rectangle [F4] makes boundary transport the identity. Multiplying around the subdivision cancels the interior edges, so the two path transports agree. The resulting section is smooth by local parallel frames, is parallel by construction, and agrees with $v_\infty$; uniqueness follows from uniqueness of parallel sections along each path. Its unit norm is preserved by unitary parallel transport, so the determinant framing reduces the structure group to $SU(N)$.

Writing $C=-F_A/(2\pi i)$, the degree-four term of $\det(I+C)$ is $c_2(A)=\tfrac12((\operatorname{tr}C)\wedge(\operatorname{tr}C)-\operatorname{tr}(C\wedge C))$. Step 2.1 gives $\operatorname{tr}F_A=0$, so this reduces to $c_2(A)=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$. Therefore $q_N=-\int_{S^4}c_2(A)$. By [F5] and the de Rham integration pairing, $\int_{S^4}c_2(A)=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$, an integer. Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. A raw framed ADHM datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its complex and real moment expressions are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\geq0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable when no nonzero subspace of $V$ is invariant under both $B_1,B_2$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular when it is both stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ and its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set

$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable and costable}\}/U(V).$$

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\mathbb R^4=S^4\setminus\{\infty\}$ is $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\to S^4$, let $E=P\times_{U(N)}\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\Phi:E|_{\infty}\to\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature matrix and define

$$q_N(P,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The anti-self-dual equation is $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$. For integer $k\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\infty$ is the identity in the framing. This definition alone does not assert that every sector exists or that $q_N$ is integral; the exact $U(N)$ charge normalization is a separate lemma below.

Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a fixed right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$. The twistor space is $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, the projection $\pi:Z\to\mathbb H\mathbb P^1=S^4$ sends a complex line $\ell$ to the quaternionic line $\ell+j\ell$, and the antiholomorphic involution is $\sigma([v])=[jv]$. A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line. Fix homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ so $\sigma$ is induced by $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. The finite real line over $z$ has equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. These equations fix the quaternionic identification and its orientation. In the chart $\lambda_1=1,\lambda_2=0$, vertical complex orientation followed by the positive orientation of $(z_1,z_2)$ is the complex orientation of $Z$.


For the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\cong SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\ell\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Use the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric for the horizontal distribution of $\pi$; the horizontal $(0,1)$ subspace at $[\ell]\in L_x$ projects to this complex alpha-plane. The displayed orientation is the twistor orientation: the vertical complex orientation followed by the quotient orientation on $S^4$ agrees with the complex orientation on $Z$. It is chosen so the curvature component that vanishes on every such plane is precisely $F^+=(F+*_gF)/2$. In spinor components, $F_{AB}=F_{(AB)}$ denotes the symmetric spinor corresponding to $F^+$ under $\Lambda^2_+T_x^*S^4\otimes\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_x^+)^*$; restriction to the plane is $F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B$, which vanishes for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ exactly when $F^+=0$.

A linear monad on $Z$ is a complex of holomorphic bundles

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

where $U,U',K$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, $b\circ a=0$, $a$ is injective as a sheaf map, $b$ is surjective, and the cohomology sheaf $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ is locally free. It is framed when that cohomology has a specified unitary trivialization on $L_\infty$. The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acts on $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$ and on $W$ by $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its raw ADHM action is

The framing torus acts on the framed monad cohomology by the same diagonal representation.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the relative Proj construction

$\mathcal O_S$-module of locally constant rank $r\ge0$
([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]). Write
$$\operatorname{Sym}(E)=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\operatorname{Sym}^d(E)$$
for the symmetric algebra of $E$
([[def-symmetric-algebra-qc-module]]): a quasi-coherent graded
$\mathcal O_S$-algebra ([[def-quasi-coherent-module-scheme]]) with $\operatorname{Sym}^0(E)=\mathcal O_S$,
$\operatorname{Sym}^1(E)=E$, generated as an $\mathcal O_S$-algebra by its
degree-one part $E$, and compatible with base change $S'\to S$
([[lem-symmetric-algebra-qc-and-base-change]]).

**Definition.** The **projective bundle** of $E$ over $S$ is the relative Proj
$$\pi:\mathbb P_S(E)=\operatorname{Proj}_S\operatorname{Sym}(E)\longrightarrow S,$$
with the relative twists $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P_S(E)}(n)$, $n\in\mathbb Z$
([[def-relative-proj-quasi-coherent-graded-algebra]]). Since
$\operatorname{Sym}(E)$ is generated in degree one, the degree-one part
$\operatorname{Sym}^1(E)=E$ generates the whole algebra, and there is a
canonical surjection
$$\pi^*E\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P_S(E)}(1),$$
the **tautological quotient** of the pullback of $E$; it is locally given by
the coordinate sections of a projective space, over an open set on which
$E\cong\mathcal O_S^{\,r}$.

**Quotient convention.** This is the quotient (Grothendieck) convention: over
an $S$-scheme $g:T\to S$, an $S$-morphism $T\to\mathbb P_S(E)$ is the same as
an isomorphism class of surjections $g^*E\to L$ with $L$ invertible on $T$,
and the universal such quotient is the tautological quotient above; the
representing property is proved as [[thm-projective-bundle-represents-line-quotients]].
The associated affine construction is
$\mathbb V(E)=\operatorname{Spec}_S\operatorname{Sym}(E)$; the rank-zero
case below displays its difference from $\mathbb P_S(E)$ over nonempty $S$.

**Rank zero.** If $E=0$ then $\operatorname{Sym}(E)=\mathcal O_S$ is
concentrated in degree $0$, its irrelevant ideal is $0$, and
$$\mathbb P_S(0)=\varnothing:$$
the total space is empty. This is consistent with the quotient convention,
because a surjection $0\to L$ onto an invertible sheaf exists only over the
empty scheme; the affine bundle $\mathbb V(0)=S$ is nonempty whenever $S$ is.

([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]), and let

be its projective bundle in the quotient convention, with twist
$\mathcal O_{\mathbb P_S(E)}(1)$ and tautological quotient

([[def-projective-bundle-scheme]],

is a natural bijection between

2. the set of isomorphism classes of surjections $g^*E\to L$ with $L$ an

([[def-base-change-map-cohomology]], [[def-higher-direct-image-sheaf]]).

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $X$ be a set and let $R \subseteq X \times X$ be a binary relation on $X$.
Call $R$ **entire on $X$** when

$$\text{for every } x \in X \text{ there is } y \in X \text{ with } x \mathbin{R} y .$$

The **Axiom of Dependent Choice**, written $\mathrm{DC}$, is the following
statement.

> For every nonempty set $X$, every relation $R$ entire on $X$, and every
> $a \in X$, there is a function $x : \mathbb{N} \to X$ (A function is a relation $f$ with $(a,b) \in f$ and $(a,c) \in f$ implying $b = c$; $f : A \to B$, the value $f(a)$, domain and codomain,
> The natural numbers $\mathbb{N}$ (von Neumann)) with
> $$x_0 = a \qquad \text{and} \qquad x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1} \ \text{ for every } n \in \mathbb{N}.$$

Here a sequence in $X$ means a function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $X$, not necessarily
a real-valued sequence. As everywhere in this library $\mathbb{N}$ contains $0$, and the sequence is
indexed from $0$; the term $x_0$ is the prescribed starting point $a$ and every
later term is related to its predecessor.

**What DC adds to what came before.** Choice function and
The Axiom of Choice select one element from each member of a family that is
fixed in advance, and The Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) does the same for a family indexed
by $\mathbb{N}$. In both, the family is given before any selection is made. DC is
the principle needed when the $n$-th set to select from is not known until the
first $n$ selections have been made: here the admissible values of $x_{n+1}$ are
exactly the $R$-successors of $x_n$, so the family being chosen from is built
along the choosing. Thus the displayed recursion is directly an instance of
DC; it is not itself an application of the fixed-family formulation of
countable choice. This observation concerns the input to the two axioms and
makes no claim about a nonimplication between them.

**The starting point may be dropped.** The formally weaker statement obtained by
deleting the clause $x_0 = a$ — for every nonempty $X$ and every entire $R$ there
is a sequence with $x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ for all $n$ — is an immediate
consequence of the form above, since $X$ is nonempty and any of its elements may
be taken as $a$. Conversely, assume the start-free form, and fix $X$, $R$ and $a$ as above. Let $P$ be the set of all functions $p:k\to X$ with nonzero $k\in\mathbb N$, $p(0)=a$, and $p(i)\mathbin R p(i+1)$ whenever $i+1<k$. It is a set by Separation inside $\mathcal P(\mathbb N\times X)$ (The power set $\mathcal{P}(x) = \{\, z : z \subseteq x \,\}$, The Cartesian product $A \times B := \{\, z \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}(A \cup B)) : \exists a \in A\ \exists b \in B\ z = (a,b) \,\}$, The Axiom Schema of Separation: for each formula $\varphi$, $\forall \bar p\,\forall x\,\exists y\,\forall z\,(z \in y \leftrightarrow (z \in x \wedge \varphi(z,\bar p)))$); a natural is the set of its predecessors (On $\mathbb{N}$ the order is membership: $m < n \iff m \in n$). The singleton path $\{(0,a)\}$ lies in $P$.

On $P$ let $p\mathbin S q$ mean that $q$ extends $p$ by exactly one new last entry. This relation is entire: for one particular $p:k\to X$, write $k=j+1$ (Every nonzero natural number is a successor); an $R$-successor $y$ of $p(j)$ exists, and $q=p\cup\{(k,y)\}$ is the required extension. This is existential instantiation for that path, not a simultaneous choice of successors. Start-free DC now supplies a sequence $(p_n)$ with $p_n\mathbin S p_{n+1}$; its first path need not be the singleton path, but every path in $P$ already starts at $a$.

Their graphs are nested. By induction (The principle of mathematical induction), $p_n$ has at least $n+1$ entries: the initial path is nonempty, and every step adds one entry. Hence $x=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}p_n$ is a function with domain $\mathbb N$ and values in $X$. Indeed, nestedness makes all common values agree, every natural index eventually lies in a path, and no path has indices outside $\mathbb N$. Each path starts at $a$, so $x(0)=a$; for any $i$, a sufficiently long path contains both $i$ and $i+1$, giving $x(i)\mathbin R x(i+1)$. Replacement and Union form this union of the sequence of graphs. Thus the start-free and prescribed-start forms are equivalent in ZF. Every use below retains the prescribed-start convention.

**$R$ need not be an order and the terms need not be distinct.** What DC delivers
is a sequence, that is a function $\mathbb{N} \to X$, not a chain in the
order-theoretic sense (Chain in a poset). The relation may be symmetric, and the
sequence may repeat a value or be constant; all that is asserted is
$x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ at every index.

derivations.claim: Algebraize the holomorphic bundle using [A1]. Its algebraic sheaf is locally free: the holomorphic bundle is dualizable, the exact tensor equivalence transports its evaluation and coevaluation and reflects their triangle identities, and those identities give a finite dual basis on each local algebraic chart, hence a finite projective module. In a splitting C⁴=A⊕B into two-planes, a graph chart of G consists of X:A→B and the incidence is (X,[λ])↦[λ,Xλ], with p a product with P(A). In the library quotient convention it is the projective bundle of the dual of the tautological subbundle. Thus [F1] gives properness, finite presentation and flatness, and e*E is a coherent locally free sheaf flat over G.

At a real line L, absolute P³ GAGA applied to the coherent algebraic sheaf i*(E|L), for the closed immersion i:L→P³, identifies its cohomology with that of the trivial analytic restriction. This uses no GAGA on the Grassmannian: closed-immersion direct image is exact, and its analytification is the same local quotient-module tensor construction. Hence the algebraic fiber cohomology is C^N in degree zero and zero above by [F3]. Its degree-one base-change map has zero target, so is surjective. By [F2] that map is an isomorphism; the finite stalk of R¹p*e*E has zero residue fiber, and Nakayama kills it on a neighborhood. The degree-one local-freeness criterion of cohomology/base change now gives surjectivity in degree zero. Evaluation p*H→e*E is a map of rank-N bundles and is invertible on L, since on its analytification it evaluates all constant sections of the trivial bundle. Its determinant-zero locus is closed. Analytify this actual evaluation isomorphism. Consequently the analytic direct image of e_an*E is H_an, its evaluation is the analytified evaluation, and all degree-zero analytic fiber maps are isomorphisms. The quaternionic involution on G sends a graph X to j_B X j_A^{-1}; its fixed graph matrices form the real four-dimensional quaternionic subspace, whose complexification is the entire graph space. derivations.claim: In the chart w=λ₂/λ₁ on a real incidence fiber, the projected horizontal (0,1) directions are H₁=∂bar_z₁−w∂z₂ and H₂=∂bar_z₂+w∂z₁. Indeed these and the vertical ∂bar_w annihilate the holomorphic coordinates w, μ₁=z₁−bar_z₂w, μ₂=z₂+bar_z₁w. They are independent and commute; their coefficients are holomorphic in w. For a unitary connection A define the pulled-back (0,1) operator by the vertical ordinary derivative and ∇_A along H₁,H₂. Its mixed squares vanish by the displayed commuting generators and holomorphic w coefficients. Its horizontal square is F_A(H₁,H₂)=F_bar1bar2−w(F_1bar1+F_2bar2)+w²F_12, which vanishes for an ASD two-form in the positive orientation: the three coefficients are precisely its self-dual component. Thus the operator squares to zero on this chart, and on the other projective chart by the same tensorial calculation. Apply [F2] to obtain a genuine holomorphic bundle. Its restriction to every real line is the constant bundle E_x, with positive reality pairing induced by the unitary metric and framing at infinity. This pairing is holomorphic: its vertical derivative vanishes on the constant fibres, and differentiating horizontally gives zero by the original identity ∇_A h=0, with the conjugate pullback at σ interchanging the conjugate horizontal directions.

For any Ward bundle use [F3] to form the analytic vector bundle H over a complex-open neighborhood U of every real line in G=Gr(2,4), with holomorphic evaluation p*H≅e*E on the universal family. On a graph chart X:A→B, incidence is (X,[λ])↦[λ,Xλ]. The distribution D=ker(de) consists of matrix variations v with vλ=0 and no λ variation. It is a holomorphic involutive rank-two subbundle, since it is tangent to the fibers of the submersion e. The restriction of p*Ω¹_U to D has kernel B*⊗O(-1) on each projective-line fiber and target D*≅O(1)². The O(-1) vanishings in [F3] give Ω¹_U≅p_*D*. Equivalently, on the graph chart a linear covector on Hom(A,B) restricts to a section on all kernels vλ=0; the map is injective because those kernels span Hom(A,B), and both coefficient spaces have dimension four. This gives the holomorphic sheaf isomorphism without any extra analytic base-change assumption.

The bundle e*E has a canonical flat partial connection δ along D: in a holomorphic frame pulled back from E, differentiate coefficient functions along the fibers of e. Changes of that frame have zero D derivative, so δ is well-defined and flat. Transfer δ to p*H by evaluation. For a local holomorphic section s of H, δ(p*s) is a section of D*⊗p*H. Push down using Ω¹_U≅p_*D* from step 2.1 to define ∇s. The partial Leibniz rule becomes ∇(fs)=df⊗s+f∇s, so ∇ is a holomorphic full connection. Its pullback restriction to D is δ, first on pulled-back sections and then on all sections by Leibniz. It is unique: the difference of two such connections is an End(H)-valued one-form restricting to zero on D at every λ, hence zero by the same cotangent isomorphism. The curvature restricts on D to δ²=0. Connections on overlapping graph charts agree by uniqueness.

Restrict H and ∇ to the totally real graph locus M=HP¹. Its smooth real incidence is diffeomorphic to Z by (P,[v])↦[v], with inverse [v]↦(span(v,jv),[v]); the explicit charts in [F3] verify smoothness. Under this identification dp(D) is exactly the span of H₁,H₂ in step 1.1: write X_z=((z₁,-bar_z₂),(z₂,bar_z₁)) and solve v(1,w)^T=0. Therefore the restricted smooth connection has F(H₁,H₂)=0 for every w, so all three self-dual coefficients in step 1.1 vanish. Hence it is ASD. Evaluation intertwines the original holomorphic operator on E with the reconstructed vertical/horizontal Dolbeault operator: it is holomorphic vertically, and on D its derivative is exactly the canonical relative derivative δ by step 3.1. These directions generate the (0,1) tangent in step 1.1, proving equality of the full operators, not just of underlying bundles.

To identify the connection with the first-neighborhood prescription, the line's conormal bundle is O(-1)², by its two independent linear defining equations. The sequence 0→E|L⊗(I/I²)→E|L^(1)→E|L→0 and [F3]'s O(-1) vanishings give a unique extension of every line section to L^(1). Smooth variation is supplied by step 3.1, not merely inferred from this pointwise uniqueness. At a graph X choose a local holomorphic section s of H with specified value and ∇s(X)=0; in a local frame its affine-linear coefficient function can realize any prescribed first jet. Its evaluation derivative in parameter direction v vanishes on vλ=0 by step 3.1, so factors through the normal displacement vλ. These factorizations glue on the two λ charts and give precisely a first-neighborhood extension. Uniqueness identifies it with the preceding extension. Subtracting such a horizontal first jet from an arbitrary section shows that differentiation relative to this extension is exactly ∇. This proves the prescription, its Leibniz rule, chart independence and smooth dependence.

The section metric is the form induced by b_z(s(z),t(σz)) in [F1]. It is independent of z on each line because that scalar is holomorphic on P¹, and is smooth by the evaluation frames of [F3]. The unitary reality pairing and framing also agree. Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. Let $k$ be a field and let $X$
be a smooth equidimensional $k$-scheme of finite type
([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]), with Chow ring $A^*(X)$
([[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]) and
vector-bundle group $K^0(X)$
([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]).
When $X$ is additionally quasi-projective,
[[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]] identifies this group with
coherent $K_0(X)$; that extra hypothesis is required for the coherent-group
extension. Write $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}:=A^*(X)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$. If $n=\dim X$,
$A^i(X)=A_{n-i}(X)=0$ for $i>n$, since there are no negative-dimensional
integral cycles. Every series below is evaluated only through degree $n$;
in particular positive-codimension elements are nilpotent. For the rank-zero
bundle the empty root list gives $\operatorname{ch}(0)=0$ and
$\operatorname{td}(0)=1$.

**Chern roots.** The **Chern roots** of a finite locally free
$\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ are formal symbols
$x_1,\dots,x_r$ with the property that the elementary symmetric functions in the
$x_i$ are the Chern classes: $e_i(x_1,\dots,x_r)=c_i(\mathcal E)$
([[def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle]]); by the splitting principle every
symmetric polynomial expression in the $x_i$ with rational coefficients defines
a well-defined element of $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$
([[lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting]]).

**Chern character.** Define
$$\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E):=\sum_{j=1}^{r}e^{x_j}=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac{1}{m!}\,p_m(c_1,\dots,c_m)\in A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q},$$
where $p_0:=r=\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E$, while for $m\ge1$ the
power sum $p_m(c_1,\dots,c_m)=\sum_jx_j^m$ is a universal polynomial in
the Chern classes. Thus $\operatorname{ch}_0(\mathcal E)=r$; explicitly
$\operatorname{ch}=r+c_1+\tfrac12(c_1^2-2c_2)+\tfrac16(c_1^3-3c_1c_2+3c_3)+\cdots$
(the denominators are why we tensor with $\mathbb Q$).

**Todd class.** Define
$$\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E):=\prod_{j=1}^{r}\frac{x_j}{1-e^{-x_j}}\in A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q};$$
explicitly
$\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E)=1+\tfrac12c_1+\tfrac1{12}(c_1^2+c_2)+\tfrac1{24}c_1c_2+\cdots$.
For a smooth $X$ the **Todd class of $X$** is $\operatorname{td}(T_X)$ for the
tangent bundle $T_X=\operatorname{Hom}(\Omega^1_{X/k},\mathcal O_X)$
([[def-sheaf-relative-differentials]],
[[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]]).

**Line bundles.** For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ with
$x=c_1(\mathcal L)$: $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal L)=e^{x}$ and
$\operatorname{td}(\mathcal L)=x/(1-e^{-x})=1+\tfrac12x+\tfrac1{12}x^2-\cdots$.

**Well-definedness.** After truncation at degree $n$, the positive-degree
components of the Chern character and all components of the Todd class are
symmetric polynomials with rational coefficients in the Chern roots, hence
universal polynomial expressions in their elementary symmetric functions,
the Chern classes of [[def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle]]. The degree-zero
component of the Chern character is the rank $r$. Thus the Chern character
depends only on the rank and Chern classes of $\mathcal E$, whereas the Todd
class depends only on its Chern classes. For locally constant ranks these
formulas are interpreted componentwise on the finite open-and-closed rank
loci. By the splitting principle of
[[lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting]], these values are
independent of the choice of flag bundle or filtration: any two filtrations
have the same rank and elementary symmetric functions, and hence give the
same polynomial values. Rational coefficients are needed for
the exponential and geometric expansions, which is why the target is
$A^*(X)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$. The tangent bundle is finite locally free
of rank $\dim X$ by [[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]], so its Chern
roots and Todd class are defined; the Todd class is multiplicative in exact sequences, whereas the Chern
character is additive, and the
identification of $K^0(X)$ with $K_0(X)$ on a quasi-projective $X$ lets the
character be evaluated on coherent classes through the finite locally free
resolutions of [[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]].

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line. the Chern classes. Thus $\operatorname{ch}_0(\mathcal E)=r$; explicitly
$\operatorname{ch}=r+c_1+\tfrac12(c_1^2-2c_2)+\tfrac16(c_1^3-3c_1c_2+3c_3)+\cdots$
(the denominators are why we tensor with $\mathbb Q$).

**Todd class.** Define
$$\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E):=\prod_{j=1}^{r}\frac{x_j}{1-e^{-x_j}}\in A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q};$$
explicitly
$\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E)=1+\tfrac12c_1+\tfrac1{12}(c_1^2+c_2)+\tfrac1{24}c_1c_2+\cdots$.
For a smooth $X$ the **Todd class of $X$** is $\operatorname{td}(T_X)$ for the
tangent bundle $T_X=\operatorname{Hom}(\Omega^1_{X/k},\mathcal O_X)$
([[def-sheaf-relative-differentials]],
[[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]]).

**Line bundles.** For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ with
$x=c_1(\mathcal L)$: $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal L)=e^{x}$ and
$\operatorname{td}(\mathcal L)=x/(1-e^{-x})=1+\tfrac12x+\tfrac1{12}x^2-\cdots$.

**Well-definedness.** After truncation at degree $n$, the positive-degree
components of the Chern character and all components of the Todd class are
symmetric polynomials with rational coefficients in the Chern roots, hence
universal polynomial expressions in their elementary symmetric functions,
the Chern classes of [[def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle]]. The degree-zero
component of the Chern character is the rank $r$. Thus the Chern character
depends only on the rank and Chern classes of $\mathcal E$, whereas the Todd
class depends only on its Chern classes. For locally constant ranks these
formulas are interpreted componentwise on the finite open-and-closed rank
loci. By the splitting principle of
[[lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting]], these values are
independent of the choice of flag bundle or filtration: any two filtrations
have the same rank and elementary symmetric functions, and hence give the
same polynomial values. Rational coefficients are needed for
the exponential and geometric expansions, which is why the target is
$A^*(X)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$. The tangent bundle is finite locally free
of rank $\dim X$ by [[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]], so its Chern
roots and Todd class are defined; the Todd class is multiplicative in exact sequences, whereas the Chern
character is additive, and the
identification of $K^0(X)$ with $K_0(X)$ on a quasi-projective $X$ lets the
character be evaluated on coherent classes through the finite locally free
resolutions of [[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]].

derivations.claim: In the Grothendieck group, exactness of the monad gives $[\mathcal E]=(2k+N)[\mathcal O]-k[\mathcal O(-1)]-k[\mathcal O(1)]$. By [F1], its Chern character is $(2k+N)-ke^{-H}-ke^H=N-kH^2$, because the constant terms cancel to $N$, the linear terms cancel, the quadratic contribution is $-kH^2$, and terms of degree at least four vanish on $Z$. Therefore $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$ and $c_2(\mathcal E)=-\operatorname{ch}_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$.

Let $x\in S^4$. In the explicit incidence chart of the Definition, $\mu_1=z_1$, $\mu_2=z_2$ at $\lambda_2=0$, so the vertical complex orientation followed by the positive stereographic orientation is the complex orientation on $Z$. The submersion pulls the oriented normal disk at $x$ back to the normal disk of its fibre; fibrewise normalization and uniqueness of the Thom class, followed by its relative-to-absolute map, therefore pull the positive point dual to the positive fibre dual. The class $u$ is Poincaré dual to the positively oriented point $x$, so $\pi^*u$ is Poincaré dual to the fibre $L_x$. By [F2] that fibre has its complex line orientation; as a linear $\mathbb CP^1\subset\mathbb CP^3$ its Poincaré dual is $H^2$, since $\int_{L_x}H=1$ and $H^2$ generates degree-four cohomology. The twistor orientation clause in the Definition makes this the positive pullback class, hence $\pi^*u=H^2$.

Write $c_2(E)=m u$ for the integer $m=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$. Naturality and the Ward pullback in the Statement give $mH^2=\pi^*c_2(E)=c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$ by step 1.1 and step 1.2. Since $H^2$ is nonzero, $m=k$. Finally [F3] gives $-q_N=m=k$, with the nonnegative sign fixed by the ASD equation.

Let $A$ be a smooth framed anti-self-dual unitary connection on the specified round oriented $S^4$, and let $\mathcal E$ be its holomorphic Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$. Suppose the following conditional Penrose-transform input is supplied for both $\mathcal E$ and its dual $\mathcal E^\vee$: there are injective linear maps

$$\mathcal P_{\mathcal E}:H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))\longrightarrow\{s\in\Gamma(E):(\nabla_A^*\nabla_A+R/8)s=0\},$$

and the analogous map for $\mathcal E^\vee$, where $R>0$ is the scalar curvature of the round metric and the target connection is the induced unitary connection. Then

$$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

This is a conditional vanishing result; it does not assert or prove the Penrose-transform input.

For $n=2$ or $3$, let $X=\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$ and let $X^{an}$ be its complex analytic space. Define analytification by $\mathcal F^{an}=\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_{X^{an}}$. It is an exact tensor-compatible equivalence from algebraic coherent sheaves (locally finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-modules) to holomorphic coherent sheaves. It identifies algebraic and holomorphic morphisms, preserves cohomology and the derived morphism groups $\operatorname{Ext}^q$, and commutes with restriction to the fixed hyperplane $L_\infty=\{z_0=0\}$. For an algebraic coherent sheaf $\mathcal E$ flat over a finite-type complex parameter scheme $S$, let $p:X\times S\to S$ be projection. Analytification commutes with the algebraic family structure and fiber restrictions. Whenever the algebraic and analytic higher direct images $R^qp_*\mathcal E$ are locally free and the natural maps from their residue-field fibers to $H^q(X_s,\mathcal E_s)$ are isomorphisms, the comparison identifies those direct images and base-change maps. No assertion is made that an arbitrary holomorphic family over a nonproper algebraic base algebraizes.

Assume full AC and DC. Let $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$, let $G=\operatorname{Gr}(2,4)$ be the complex Grassmannian of projective lines in $Z$, and let $p:\mathscr L\to G$ be the universal line family with evaluation map $e:\mathscr L\to Z$. Let $\mathcal E\to Z$ be a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle, $N\geq2$, with a positive Hermitian real structure and a unitary framing on the twistor line at $\infty$. Assume its restriction to every real twistor line $L_x$ is holomorphically and unitarily trivial. The degree-zero base-change maps at every real line are isomorphisms. Then $(p_*e^*\mathcal E)|_{S^4}$ is a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle, its fibre at $x$ is $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$, and the evaluation morphism identifies its pullback to the real incidence family with $e^*\mathcal E$. More precisely, for every real line, there is a complex-open neighbourhood in $G$ on whose entire universal-line family the evaluation morphism is an isomorphism. The framing on $L_\infty$ induces a unitary framing of this bundle at $\infty$.

Assume full AC and the exact projective GAGA comparison used below; its substantial local analytic prerequisites remain unresolved in its own carrier. The local smooth integrable-Dolbeault frame theorem is supplied by the explicit local proof, rather than assumed as a new analytic input.

For $N\geq2$, let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ be the framed unitary ASD sector on the round oriented $S^4$ defined above. On the Ward side take a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum, and a unitary framing on $L_\infty$. Require $\mathcal E|_{L_x}\cong\mathcal O_{L_x}^{\oplus N}$ for every real twistor line, and require $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$, where $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$. Then $\widehat E_x=H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ forms a smooth rank-$N$ Hermitian bundle on $S^4$. For each section of $\widehat E_x$, extend it holomorphically and uniquely to the first infinitesimal neighbourhood of $L_x$ and differentiate this extension in the family of lines; this defines the Ward connection $\widehat\nabla$. The form induced by the positive holomorphic reality pairing is smooth and is preserved by $\widehat\nabla$; this is a conclusion, not an independent metric-compatibility assumption.

Under these hypotheses, the Ward construction gives a bijection between based unitary gauge classes in $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ and isomorphism classes of the specified framed Ward bundles. The reconstructed Ward connection satisfies $F^+=0$ and $q_N=-k$. The inverse sends a framed ASD connection to the holomorphic structure on $\pi^*E$ whose vertical part is the standard Dolbeault operator and whose horizontal $(0,1)$ part is the connection on the planes $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Both maps preserve the framing, Hermitian form, charge, and compact torus action. Reducible bundles and flat summands are included; no irreducibility assumption is imposed.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle with $N\geq2$, a smooth unitary connection $A$, and a unitary framing at $\infty$. Give $S^4$ the round metric and the orientation specified in the definition of the framed ASD sector, and assume $F_A^+=0$. Then the induced determinant-line connection on $\det E=\Lambda^N E$ is flat. Its framing at $\infty$ determines a unique global unit parallel section, so the framed unitary bundle reduces to a framed $SU(N)$ bundle. With $q_N=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$ and the determinant Chern-form convention $c(A)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$, one has

$$q_N(E,A)=-\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle\in-\mathbb Z_{\geq0}.$$

Thus $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$ is a nonnegative integer, with the sign corresponding to the anti-self-dual equation $F_A^+=0$.

Let $A$ be a smooth framed anti-self-dual unitary connection on the specified round oriented $S^4$, and let $\mathcal E$ be its holomorphic Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$. Suppose the following conditional Penrose-transform input is supplied for both $\mathcal E$ and its dual $\mathcal E^\vee$: there are injective linear maps

$$\mathcal P_{\mathcal E}:H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))\longrightarrow\{s\in\Gamma(E):(\nabla_A^*\nabla_A+R/8)s=0\},$$

and the analogous map for $\mathcal E^\vee$, where $R>0$ is the scalar curvature of the round metric and the target connection is the induced unitary connection. Then

$$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

This is a conditional vanishing result; it does not assert or prove the Penrose-transform input.

Let $E	o S^4$ be a finite-rank Hermitian vector bundle with a smooth unitary connection $
abla$, where $S^4$ is the unit round sphere with no boundary. Let $c>0$ be a real constant. If a smooth section $s\in\Gamma(E)$ satisfies $(
abla^*
abla+cI)s=0$, where $
abla^*$ is the formal adjoint for the round volume and Hermitian metric, then $s=0$.
For every natural number $n\ge2$, the unit sphere $S^n\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$ is simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]).

A connection on a finite-rank smooth vector bundle $E\to M$ is flat if and
only if every point of $M$ has a neighborhood carrying a local frame
$(e_1,\ldots,e_r)$ of parallel sections, meaning $\nabla_Xe_a=0$ for every
local vector field $X$ and every $a$.

Let $E\to M$ carry a flat connection, meaning $R^\nabla=0$. For every
$p\in M$ there is a coordinate ball $U$ about $p$ such that, whenever two
piecewise smooth paths $\gamma_0,\gamma_1:[0,1]\to U$ have the same initial
and terminal points,

$$P_{\gamma_0}=P_{\gamma_1}.$$

This is a local assertion; it makes no claim about transport around loops in a
non-simply-connected larger domain.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. A section $s$ of a rank-$d$
bundle $Q$ is a **regular section** here if, at each point of its zero scheme
$Z(s)$, some local frame expresses $s$ by $d$ components forming a regular
sequence of length $d$ in the local ring. Under this hypothesis it has exact
Koszul resolution
$\bigwedge^dQ^\vee\to\cdots\to Q^\vee\to\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_{Z(s)}\to0$.
Tensoring with a vector bundle preserves it. If a coherent sheaf $H$ has a
finite locally free resolution on a scheme and $t$ is a Cartier equation acting
injectively on $H$, restricting the resolution to $t=0$ remains exact and
resolves $H/tH$. In the deformation blowup for a closed embedding of smooth
quasi-projective varieties $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$, let $E$ be a finite
locally free sheaf on $X$. The strict transform
$F:X\times\mathbb P^1\hookrightarrow M$ is disjoint from
$B=\operatorname{Bl}_XY$, and a resolution of $F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$
restricts exactly to the ordinary $Y$ fibre and to
$P=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(N\oplus1)$; on $B$ it is an exact complex.

For an additive left-exact functor $F$ and a bounded-below complex $K$ with supplied Cartan–Eilenberg resolution $I$, there is a spectral sequence
$$E_1^{p,q}=R^qF(K^p)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathbb R_I^{p+q}F(K),\qquad d_r:(p,q)\mapsto(p+r,q-r+1).$$
Here $q\ge0$ and $p\ge b$ if $K^p=0$ for $p<b$. It is first quadrant after translating $p$ by $b$ and converges strongly with a finite filtration on every target degree. Derived objects use the supplied columns; under DC, or supplied Cartan–Eilenberg comparison and homotopy data, it is natural in $K$ and independent of the resolution from $E_1$ onward.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and $n\ge0$, let
$X=\mathbb P^n_k$ with dualizing line bundle $\omega_X=\mathcal O(-n-1)$ and
residue trace $t_X:H^n(X,\omega_X)\to k$
([[def-smooth-projective-dualizing-line-bundle-and-trace]]), and let
$\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}$ be the global sheaf Ext of
[[def-sheaf-ext-for-coherent-modules]].

1. **(The pairing.)** For every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$, every
   $q\in\{0,\dots,n\}$, $\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)$
   and $\eta\in H^q(X,F)$ set
   $$\langle\alpha,\eta\rangle_F\;:=\;t_X\Bigl(\chi^n_{\omega_X}\bigl(\alpha\cdot\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)\bigr)\Bigr),$$
   where $\chi^q_F:\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q(X,F)$
   is the canonical isomorphism of
   [[lem-injective-modules-flasque-and-ext-of-structure-sheaf]],
   $\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)$ is the corresponding class in
   $\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,F)$, and
   $\alpha\cdot\beta\in\operatorname{Ext}^n_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,\omega_X)$
   is the Yoneda product of
   $\alpha\in\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)$ with
   $\beta=\chi^q_F{}^{-1}(\eta)$, i.e. composition
   $\alpha\circ\beta$ of derived morphisms under
   $\operatorname{Ext}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal O_X}(-,-)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X))}(-,-[\bullet])$
   ([[thm-ext-is-hom-in-the-derived-category]],
   [[prop-yoneda-product-is-composition-in-the-derived-category]]). This
   **Serre duality pairing** is $k$-bilinear and natural in $F$.

2. **(Perfectness.)** For every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ and every
   $q\in\{0,\dots,n\}$ the pairing
   $$\langle-,-\rangle_F:\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\times H^q(X,F)\longrightarrow k$$
   is a perfect pairing of $k$-vector spaces, i.e. both adjoint maps
   $\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\to H^q(X,F)^\vee$ and
   $H^q(X,F)\to\operatorname{Ext}^{n-q}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)^\vee$ are
   isomorphisms.

The case $q=n$ of clause 2 is the classical statement that
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\to H^n(X,F)^\vee$,
$\varphi\mapsto(\eta\mapsto t_X(H^n(\varphi)(\eta)))$, is an isomorphism, and
for $F=\mathcal O_X$ clause 2 recovers $H^{n-q}(X,\omega_X)\cong H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)^\vee$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring with $1$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]), let $n\ge0$, let $d\in\mathbb Z$ and
let $X=\mathbb P^n_A\cong\operatorname{Proj}A[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be relative
projective space ([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]],
[[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]), with twisting sheaf
$\mathcal O_X(d)$ ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]]) and cohomology
$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$. Then
$$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0\qquad\text{unless }q=0\text{ or }q=n.$$
If $n>0$, then $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ when $d\ge0$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0$ when $d<0$, where
$A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ is the degree-$d$ graded piece
([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]); and $H^n(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ is the
free $A$-module on the Laurent monomials $x_0^{e_0}\cdots x_n^{e_n}$ with
$e_i<0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_ie_i=d$, so that it is nonzero precisely when
$d\le-n-1$ and $A\ne0$. For $n=0$ one has $\mathbb P^0_A=\operatorname{Spec}A$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A$ for every $d\in\mathbb Z$, with all higher
groups zero. The zero ring $A=0$ is allowed: then $X=\varnothing$ and all
groups are zero, in agreement with both displayed descriptions.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. Let $k$ be an algebraically
closed field, let $Y$ be a nonsingular equidimensional quasi-projective
$k$-scheme of finite type ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]],
[[cor-smooth-variety-classical-scheme-conventions-agree]]), let $n\ge0$ and let
$$p:\mathbb P^n_k\times_kY\longrightarrow Y$$
be the projection. For every
$\alpha\in K_0(\mathbb P^n\times_kY)$
([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]):
$$\operatorname{ch}\bigl(p_!(\alpha)\bigr)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_Y)\;=\;p_*\Bigl(\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n\times_kY})\Bigr)\qquad\text{in }A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q},$$
where $\operatorname{ch},\operatorname{td}$ are the Chern character and Todd
class of [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]], $p_!$ is the K-theory
pushforward ([[def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory]],
[[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]]) and $p_*$ is the proper
pushforward on Chow groups
([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]). Equivalently, writing
$\tau_X(\alpha)=\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\operatorname{td}(T_X)$, the diagram
$$\begin{array}{ccc}K_0(\mathbb P^n\times_kY) & \xrightarrow{\ \tau\ } & A^*(\mathbb P^n\times_kY)_{\mathbb Q}\\ \downarrow p_! & & \downarrow p_*\\ K_0(Y) & \xrightarrow{\ \tau\ } & A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}\end{array}$$
commutes. The case $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch for
$\mathbb P^n$, and the case of a general projective-bundle projection is obtained
by the same argument applied to the projective bundle formula.

derivations.claim: By [A1] and [F1], the image of every class in $H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))$ is a solution of the coupled Laplace equation with positive scalar term, hence is zero; injectivity makes the class zero. Applying the same argument to $\mathcal E^\vee$ gives $H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0$. This argument includes reducible connections.

Let $L\cong\mathbb P^1$ be any real twistor line. Its normal bundle in $\mathbb P^3$ is $\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$, and the conormal sequence splits because its extension group is $H^1(\mathcal O(1))^{\oplus2}=0$. Hence $\Omega_Z^1|_L\cong\mathcal O(-2)\oplus\mathcal O(-1)^{\oplus2}$ and $T_Z|_L\cong\mathcal O(2)\oplus\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$. Since $\Omega_Z^2\cong T_Z(-4)$, each of $\mathcal E(-1)|_L$, $\mathcal E(-3)|_L$, $\mathcal E(-2)|_L$, $(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))|_L$, and $(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)|_L$ is a sum of negative line bundles. The Serre-dual bundles restrict respectively to $\mathcal E^*(-3)$, $\mathcal E^*(-1)$, $\mathcal E^*(-2)$, $\mathcal E^*\otimes T_Z(-3)$, and $\mathcal E^*\otimes\Omega_Z^1$, also sums of negative line bundles. Every point of $Z$ lies on a real line, so negativity on every such line makes every global section zero. Thus [F6] gives $H^0(Z,F)=0$ and [F5] gives $H^3(Z,F)=0$ for all the listed coefficient bundles $F$.

Choose a plane $P\cong\mathbb P^2$ containing a real twistor line. By [A2] and the direct-image result, an open family of lines near that line has evaluation isomorphisms and hence trivial restrictions of $\mathcal E$. Those lines form a nonempty open subset of the line family of $P$; the incidence projection from this open subset covers a dense subset of $P$. A section of $\mathcal E(-2)|_P$ vanishes on every such line because $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus N})=0$, so it vanishes on a dense subset and is zero. The divisor sequence $0\to\mathcal E(-3)\to\mathcal E(-2)\to\mathcal E(-2)|_P\to0$ and step 1.1 now give $H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-3))=0$.

Tensor $0\to\Omega_Z^1(-1)\to\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus4}\to\mathcal O(-1)\to0$ by $\mathcal E$. Step 1.2 gives $H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=H^0(\mathcal E(-1))=0$, and step 1.1 gives $H^1(\mathcal E(-2))=0$. The long exact sequence yields $H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))=0$. Serre duality and step 1.1 also give $H^2(\mathcal E(-2))=0$.

Apply [F4] to the diagonal Koszul resolution [F3], tensoring the second factor by $\mathcal E(-2)$, pushing to the first factor, and twisting that output factor by $\mathcal O(2)$. Its first page is $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(Z,\mathcal E(-2)\otimes\Omega_Z^{-p}(-p))\otimes\mathcal O_Z(p+2)$ for $p=-3,-2,-1,0$. Steps 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 and Serre duality make every term in rows $q=0,1,3$ vanish except possibly $H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)$ at $(-2,1)$. No differential can enter this term; its only possible outgoing $d_2$ lands in $H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=0$. It therefore survives to $E_\infty$, but the diagonal complex resolves $\mathcal E(-2)$ in degree zero and has no degree $-1$ hypercohomology. Since $(-2)+1=-1$, the term is zero. Thus the remaining spectral-sequence row is $q=2$.

The row $q=2$ gives the complex $H^2(\mathcal E(-3))\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)\otimes\mathcal O\to H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))\otimes\mathcal O(1)$. All higher differentials vanish because all other rows are zero. The maps are linear in the homogeneous output coordinates, since each Koszul differential is contraction with the universal linear section. Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy the raw complex equation $\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Put $K=V\oplus V\oplus W$. For $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$ put

$$a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T,\qquad b_z=(-B_2^\dagger+\bar z_2,B_1^\dagger-\bar z_1,I^\dagger)^T,\qquad D_z=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger\\a_z^\dagger\end{pmatrix}.$$

Then

$$D_zD_z^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger b_z&\mu_{\mathbb C}\\\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger&a_z^\dagger a_z\end{pmatrix},\qquad b_z^\dagger b_z-a_z^\dagger a_z=\mu_{\mathbb R}.$$

The maps $b_z^\dagger$ are onto for every $z$ exactly when the datum is stable; the maps $a_z$ are injective for every $z$ exactly when it is costable. Consequently, when both moments vanish, regularity is equivalent to $D_z$ being onto for every $z$. On this locus $f_z=a_z^\dagger a_z=b_z^\dagger b_z$ is positive definite and

$$P_z=1-D_z^\dagger\operatorname{diag}(f_z^{-1},f_z^{-1})D_z$$

is the smooth orthogonal projection onto a rank-$N$ bundle over $\mathbb R^4$. The projection connection $\nabla=P\,d$ is unitary and satisfies $F^+=0$ for the positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$.

In homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ on $\mathbb P^3$, put $A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1$, $C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2$ and

$$\alpha=(A,C,J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2)^T,\qquad\beta=(-C,A,I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2).$$

The polynomial identity is $\beta\alpha=\lambda_1^2\mu_{\mathbb C}+\lambda_1\lambda_2\mu_{\mathbb R}-\lambda_2^2\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger$. With $\sigma(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$, one has $\beta(v)=\alpha(\sigma v)^\dagger$. The real line over $z$ is $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. For regular zero-moment data these maps form a holomorphic bundle monad, trivial on each real line, with middle cohomology on the line over $z$ canonically $\ker D_z$. Its framing at infinity is $W$. The torus acts on the homogeneous coordinates by $(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ and on the raw data by $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$; the monad isomorphism has source, middle and target factors $(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$ and $1$, respectively. It preserves the framing representation $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$.

This proves a forward raw block construction. It does not assert that every real Ward monad has this normal form, that its inverse extraction is unique, or that the connection extends with charge $k$; those global correspondence and charge assertions require their separate proofs.

Let $A$ be a framed unitary ASD connection on the round oriented $S^4$, let $\mathcal E$ be its Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$, and let $k=-q_N(A)$. Assume the conditional Penrose-transform input stated in the next paragraph for both $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal E^\vee$. Assume also the exact projective GAGA and line-family base-change inputs needed to regard $\mathcal E$ as an algebraic bundle, to make its restrictions trivial on a complex-open neighbourhood of at least one real twistor line, and to apply the diagonal resolution. Finally, use the Chern-character normalization $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$ in $A^*(\mathbb CP^3)_\mathbb Q$, where $H=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$; this normalization is conditional on the twistor pullback class convention matching the framed charge.

Under these inputs,

$$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

There is a canonical Beilinson three-term monad

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

whose middle cohomology is $\mathcal E$ and whose terms are

$$U=H^2(Z,\mathcal E(-3)),\qquad K=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2),\qquad U'=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1)),$$

with $\dim U=\dim U'=k$ and $\dim K=2k+N$. The construction is natural in framed bundle isomorphisms and unique up to changes of bases in $U,K,U'$. The values of all global parallel sections form its maximal trivial flat parallel summand, and the connection splits orthogonally into that summand and a summand with no nonzero parallel sections; arbitrary nonflat parallel summands are permitted. The monad construction is additive across this splitting and uses no hypothesis $H^0(Z,\mathcal E)=0$.

Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. Let $\pi:Z=\mathbb CP^3\to S^4$ be the oriented twistor fibration with the conventions stated in the following references section, let $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$, and let $E\to S^4$ be a framed unitary ASD rank-$N$ bundle whose Ward bundle is $\mathcal E=\pi^*E$ as a smooth bundle. $$\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\oplus k}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus(2k+N)}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)^{\oplus k}.$$

$$k=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-q_N(E,A).$$

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle with $N\geq2$, a smooth unitary connection $A$, and a unitary framing at $\infty$. real coefficients; no equality with integral torsion is asserted.
